sanskrit: nāradaḥ parvataś caiva mahātmānau mahāvratau devarājasya bhavanaṃ viviśāte supūjitau
english: Nārada and Parvata, both great-souled and of mighty vows, entered the abode of the king of gods, and were received with great honour.

sanskrit: tāv arcitvā sahasrākṣas tataḥ kuśalam avyayam papracchānāmayaṃ cāpi tayoḥ sarvagataṃ vibhuḥ
english: Having worshipped them, the thousand-eyed lord, the all-pervading one, then asked them of their welfare and enquired also about the health of all in every place.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca āvayoḥ kuśalaṃ deva sarvatragatam īśvara loke ca maghavan kṛtsne nṛpāḥ kuśalino vibho
english: Nārada said: O god, O lord, our welfare extends everywhere; and O Maghavan, O all-powerful one, the kings throughout the entire world are prospering.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā papraccha balavṛtrahā dharmajñāḥ pṛthivīpālās tyaktajīvitayodhinaḥ
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Having heard Nārada's words, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra asked about those kings who know righteousness and who fight having cast off all attachment to life.

sanskrit: śastreṇa nidhanaṃ kāle ye gacchanty aparāṅmukhāḥ ayaṃ loko 'kṣayas teṣāṃ yathaiva mama kāmadhuk
english: Those who meet their death by weapons at the proper time, without turning their backs in battle — for them this world is imperishable, just as it fulfils all my desires.

sanskrit: kva nu te kṣatriyāḥ śūrā na hi paśyāmi tān aham āgacchato mahīpālān atithīn dayitān mama
english: Where now are those heroic warriors? I do not see them here. The kings who used to come as beloved guests to my dwelling — where are they?

sanskrit: evam uktas tu śakreṇa nāradaḥ pratyabhāṣata śṛṇu me bhagavan yena na dṛśyante mahīkṣitaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Śakra, Nārada replied: Hear me, O blessed lord — I shall tell you why those rulers of the earth are not to be seen here.

sanskrit: vidarbharājaduhitā damayantīti viśrutā rūpeṇa samatikrāntā pṛthivyāṃ sarvayoṣitaḥ
english: The daughter of the king of Vidarbha, renowned as Damayantī, has surpassed all women on earth in beauty.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ svayaṃvaraḥ śakra bhavitā nacirād iva tatra gacchanti rājāno rājaputrāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: O Śakra, her svayaṃvara will take place very soon; kings and princes are all going there from every direction.

sanskrit: tāṃ ratnabhūtāṃ lokasya prārthayanto mahīkṣitaḥ kāṅkṣanti sma viśeṣeṇa balavṛtraniṣūdana
english: Desiring her who is a jewel of the world, the rulers of the earth are longing for her especially, O slayer of Bala and Vṛtra.

sanskrit: etasmin kathyamāne tu lokapālāś ca sāgnikāḥ ājagmur devarājasya samīpam amarottamāḥ
english: While this was being told, the guardian deities of the worlds, together with Agni, came — those best among the immortals — to the presence of the king of gods.

sanskrit: tatas tac chuśruvuḥ sarve nāradasya vaco mahat śrutvā caivābruvan hṛṣṭā gacchāmo vayam apy uta
english: Then all of them heard Nārada's important words, and having heard, they said joyfully: Let us also go there.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve mahārāja sagaṇāḥ sahavāhanāḥ vidarbhān abhito jagmur yatra sarve mahīkṣitaḥ
english: Then all of them, O great king, along with their retinues and their vehicles, set out toward Vidarbha, where all the earthly kings were headed.

sanskrit: nalo 'pi rājā kaunteya śrutvā rājñāṃ samāgamam abhyagacchad adīnātmā damayantīm anuvrataḥ
english: King Nala too, O son of Kuntī, having heard of the assembly of kings, set out with undaunted spirit, devoted to Damayantī.

sanskrit: atha devāḥ pathi nalaṃ dadṛśur bhūtale sthitam sākṣād iva sthitaṃ mūrtyā manmathaṃ rūpasaṃpadā
english: Then the gods on the way saw Nala standing on the earth — his beauty making him seem like the god of love himself standing there in bodily form.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā lokapālās te bhrājamānaṃ yathā ravim tasthur vigatasaṃkalpā vismitā rūpasaṃpadā
english: Seeing him radiant as the sun, those guardians of the worlds stood still, their purposes forgotten, astonished at the perfection of his form.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe viṣṭabhya vimānāni divaukasaḥ abruvan naiṣadhaṃ rājann avatīrya nabhastalāt
english: Then the celestial beings, having stationed their aerial cars in the sky, descended from the heavens and spoke to the king of Niṣadha.

sanskrit: bho bho naiṣadha rājendra nala satyavrato bhavān asmākaṃ kuru sāhāyyaṃ dūto bhava narottama
english: Ho, ho, Naiṣadha, king of kings! You, Nala, are a man of true vows. Do us a service — be our messenger, O best of men.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca tebhyaḥ pratijñāya nalaḥ kariṣya iti bhārata athainān paripapraccha kṛtāñjalir avasthitaḥ
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Having promised them "I shall do it," O Bhārata, Nala then stood with palms joined and asked them further.

sanskrit: ke vai bhavantaḥ kaś cāsau yasyāhaṃ dūta īpsitaḥ kiṃ ca tatra mayā kāryaṃ kathayadhvaṃ yathātatham
english: Who indeed are you? And who is that person whose messenger I am desired to be? And what task must I do there? Tell me everything exactly as it is.

sanskrit: evam ukte naiṣadhena maghavān pratyabhāṣata amarān vai nibodhāsmān damayantyartham āgatān
english: When the king of Niṣadha spoke thus, Maghavān replied: Know us indeed to be immortals who have come on account of Damayantī.

sanskrit: aham indro 'yam agniś ca tathaivāyam apāṃpatiḥ śarīrāntakaro nṝṇāṃ yamo 'yam api pārthiva
english: I am Indra; here is Agni; and likewise here is the lord of waters; and this is Yama, the ender of men's bodies, O king.

sanskrit: sa vai tvam āgatān asmān damayantyai nivedaya lokapālāḥ sahendrās tvāṃ samāyānti didṛkṣavaḥ
english: Therefore announce our arrival to Damayantī: the guardians of the worlds together with Indra are coming, desiring to see her.

sanskrit: prāptum icchanti devās tvāṃ śakro 'gnir varuṇo yamaḥ teṣām anyatamaṃ devaṃ patitve varayasva ha
english: Śakra, Agni, Varuṇa, and Yama — the gods desire to obtain her; let her choose one among these gods as her husband.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa śakreṇa nalaḥ prāñjalir abravīt ekārthasamavetaṃ māṃ na preṣayitum arhatha
english: Thus addressed by Śakra, Nala said with joined palms: You ought not to send me on a mission that concerns the very same purpose that brings me there.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ kariṣya iti saṃśrutya pūrvam asmāsu naiṣadha na kariṣyasi kasmāt tvaṃ vraja naiṣadha māciram
english: The gods said: Having previously promised us "I shall do it," why now, O Naiṣadha, will you not do it? Go, Naiṣadha, do not delay.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evam uktaḥ sa devais tair naiṣadhaḥ punar abravīt surakṣitāni veśmāni praveṣṭuṃ katham utsahe
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Thus urged by those gods, the king of Niṣadha replied again: How can I dare to enter her well-guarded chambers?

sanskrit: pravekṣyasīti taṃ śakraḥ punar evābhyabhāṣata jagāma sa tathety uktvā damayantyā niveśanam
english: "You shall enter," Śakra said to him again; and he, saying "so be it," went to Damayantī's dwelling.

sanskrit: dadarśa tatra vaidarbhīṃ sakhīgaṇasamāvṛtām dedīpyamānāṃ vapuṣā śriyā ca varavarṇinīm
english: There he saw the princess of Vidarbha surrounded by her circle of friends, blazing with her bodily beauty and splendour, that excellent-complexioned one.

sanskrit: atīva sukumārāṅgīṃ tanumadhyāṃ sulocanām ākṣipantīm iva ca bhāḥ śaśinaḥ svena tejasā
english: Her limbs were supremely tender, her waist was slender, her eyes most beautiful — and with her own radiance she seemed to snatch away even the light of the moon.

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvaiva vavṛdhe kāmas tāṃ cāruhāsinīm satyaṃ cikīrṣamāṇas tu dhārayām āsa hṛcchayam
english: On seeing her, that lovely-smiling one, desire grew within him; but wishing to keep his promise true, he restrained the longing of his heart.

sanskrit: tatas tā naiṣadhaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃbhrāntāḥ paramāṅganāḥ āsanebhyaḥ samutpetus tejasā tasya dharṣitāḥ
english: Then those most excellent women, seeing the king of Niṣadha, rose up startled from their seats, overpowered by his radiance.

sanskrit: praśaśaṃsuś ca suprītā nalaṃ tā vismayānvitāḥ na cainam abhyabhāṣanta manobhis tv abhyacintayan
english: Full of delight and wonder, they praised Nala, yet could not bring themselves to address him; they only contemplated him in their minds.

sanskrit: aho rūpam aho kāntir aho dhairyaṃ mahātmanaḥ ko 'yaṃ devo nu yakṣo nu gandharvo nu bhaviṣyati
english: "What beauty! What charm! What composure this great-souled one possesses! Is he a god, or a yakṣa, or a gandharva?"

sanskrit: na tv enaṃ śaknuvanti sma vyāhartum api kiṃ cana tejasā dharṣitāḥ sarvā lajjāvatyo varāṅganāḥ
english: But all those lovely, modest women, overpowered by his radiance, were unable to say anything at all to him.

sanskrit: athainaṃ smayamāneva smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇī damayantī nalaṃ vīram abhyabhāṣata vismitā
english: Then Damayantī, astonished, smiled slightly and, as one who speaks first with a smile, addressed the hero Nala.

sanskrit: kas tvaṃ sarvānavadyāṅga mama hṛcchayavardhana prāpto 'sy amaravad vīra jñātum icchāmi te 'nagha
english: "Who are you, O one whose limbs are altogether faultless, O increaser of the longing in my heart? You have come like an immortal, O hero — I wish to know you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: katham āgamanaṃ ceha kathaṃ cāsi na lakṣitaḥ surakṣitaṃ hi me veśma rājā caivograśāsanaḥ
english: "How did you come here? And how were you not noticed? My chambers are well-guarded, and the king too is one of fierce commands."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vaidarbhyā nalas tāṃ pratyuvāca ha nalaṃ māṃ viddhi kalyāṇi devadūtam ihāgatam
english: Thus addressed by the princess of Vidarbha, Nala replied to her: Know me to be Nala, O auspicious one, come here as a messenger of the gods.

sanskrit: devās tvāṃ prāptum icchanti śakro 'gnir varuṇo yamaḥ teṣām anyatamaṃ devaṃ patiṃ varaya śobhane
english: "The gods desire to obtain you — Śakra, Agni, Varuṇa, and Yama. O beautiful one, choose one among them as your husband."

sanskrit: teṣām eva prabhāvena praviṣṭo 'ham alakṣitaḥ praviśantaṃ hi māṃ kaś cin nāpaśyan nāpy avārayat
english: "By their divine power alone I entered unseen; as I entered, no one saw me and no one barred my way."

sanskrit: etadartham ahaṃ bhadre preṣitaḥ surasattamaiḥ etac chrutvā śubhe buddhiṃ prakuruṣva yathecchasi
english: "For this purpose I was sent by those best of gods, O fortunate one. Having heard this, O auspicious one, make up your mind as you wish."

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca sā namaskṛtya devebhyaḥ prahasya nalam abravīt praṇayasva yathāśraddhaṃ rājan kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: Bṛhadaśva said: She, having paid homage to the gods, said laughingly to Nala: O king, show your affection as you trust — what shall I do for you?

sanskrit: ahaṃ caiva hi yac cānyan mamāsti vasu kiṃ cana sarvaṃ tat tava viśrabdhaṃ kuru praṇayam īśvara
english: "I myself, and whatever other wealth of mine there is — all of that is yours with confidence; show your desire, O lord."

sanskrit: haṃsānāṃ vacanaṃ yat tat tan māṃ dahati pārthiva tvatkṛte hi mayā vīra rājānaḥ saṃnipātitāḥ
english: "That message of the swans burns within me, O king; it is for your sake, O hero, that I have assembled all these kings."

sanskrit: yadi ced bhajamānāṃ māṃ pratyākhyāsyasi mānada viṣam agniṃ jalaṃ rajjum āsthāsye tava kāraṇāt
english: "If you should reject me who am devoted to you, O bestower of honour, I shall resort to poison, fire, water, or a rope — on your account."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vaidarbhyā nalas tāṃ pratyuvāca ha tiṣṭhatsu lokapāleṣu kathaṃ mānuṣam icchasi
english: Thus addressed by the princess of Vidarbha, Nala replied to her: With the guardians of the worlds present, how can you desire a mortal?

sanskrit: yeṣām ahaṃ lokakṛtām īśvarāṇāṃ mahātmanām na pādarajasā tulyo manas te teṣu vartatām
english: "I am not even equal to the dust of the feet of those great-souled lords, the creators of the worlds. Let your mind dwell on them."

sanskrit: vipriyaṃ hy ācaran martyo devānāṃ mṛtyum ṛcchati trāhi mām anavadyāṅgi varayasva surottamān
english: "A mortal who acts contrary to the gods' wishes meets his death. Protect me, O you of faultless limbs, and choose those best among the gods."

sanskrit: tato bāṣpakalāṃ vācaṃ damayantī śucismitā pravyāharantī śanakair nalaṃ rājānam abravīt
english: Then Damayantī, whose smile was pure, her voice laden with tears, spoke slowly to king Nala.

sanskrit: asty upāyo mayā dṛṣṭo nirapāyo nareśvara yena doṣo na bhavitā tava rājan kathaṃ cana
english: "There is a means I have devised, O lord of men — a flawless means, O king, by which no blame will fall on you in any way."

sanskrit: tvaṃ caiva hi naraśreṣṭha devāś cāgnipurogamāḥ āyāntu sahitāḥ sarve mama yatra svayaṃvaraḥ
english: "You, O best of men, and the gods with Agni at their head — let all of them come together to the place of my svayaṃvara."

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ lokapālānāṃ saṃnidhau tvāṃ nareśvara varayiṣye naravyāghra naivaṃ doṣo bhaviṣyati
english: "Then in the presence of the guardians of the worlds I shall choose you, O lord of men, O tiger among men — thus no blame will arise."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu vaidarbhyā nalo rājā viśāṃ pate ājagāma punas tatra yatra devāḥ samāgatāḥ
english: Thus addressed by the princess of Vidarbha, king Nala, O lord of people, returned again to the place where the gods had assembled.

sanskrit: tam apaśyaṃs tathāyāntaṃ lokapālāḥ saheśvarāḥ dṛṣṭvā cainaṃ tato 'pṛcchan vṛttāntaṃ sarvam eva tat
english: The guardians of the worlds together with their lord saw him coming thus; having seen him, they asked him about everything that had transpired.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ kaccid dṛṣṭā tvayā rājan damayantī śucismitā kim abravīc ca naḥ sarvān vada bhūmipate 'nagha
english: The gods said: O king, did you see Damayantī of the pure smile? What did she say to us all? Tell us, O lord of the earth, O sinless one.

sanskrit: nala uvāca bhavadbhir aham ādiṣṭo damayantyā niveśanam praviṣṭaḥ sumahākakṣyaṃ daṇḍibhiḥ sthavirair vṛtam
english: Nala said: Commanded by you, I entered the dwelling of Damayantī — that very great enclosure surrounded by staff-bearing elders.

sanskrit: praviśantaṃ ca māṃ tatra na kaś cid dṛṣṭavān naraḥ ṛte tāṃ pārthivasutāṃ bhavatām eva tejasā
english: "And as I entered there, no man saw me, except that princess — by your divine power alone."

sanskrit: sakhyaś cāsyā mayā dṛṣṭās tābhiś cāpy upalakṣitaḥ vismitāś cābhavan dṛṣṭvā sarvā māṃ vibudheśvarāḥ
english: "Her friends too I saw, and they in turn noticed me; on seeing me, O lords of the gods, all of them became astonished."

sanskrit: varṇyamāneṣu ca mayā bhavatsu rucirānanā mām eva gatasaṃkalpā vṛṇīte surasattamāḥ
english: "And even as I was describing you to her, that lovely-faced one has fixed her resolve upon me alone. She will choose me, O best among gods."

sanskrit: abravīc caiva māṃ bālā āyāntu sahitāḥ surāḥ tvayā saha naraśreṣṭha mama yatra svayaṃvaraḥ
english: "And the young woman said to me: Let the gods come together, along with you, O best of men, to the place of my svayaṃvara."

sanskrit: teṣām ahaṃ saṃnidhau tvāṃ varayiṣye narottama evaṃ tava mahābāho doṣo na bhaviteti ha
english: "'In their presence I shall choose you, O best of men — thus, O mighty-armed one, no blame will fall upon you,' she said."

sanskrit: etāvad eva vibudhā yathāvṛttam udāhṛtam mayāśeṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ tu bhavantas tridaśeśvarāḥ
english: "This is all that happened, recounted by me as it truly occurred; you, O lords of the thirty gods, are the final authority in this matter."

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca atha kāle śubhe prāpte tithau puṇye kṣaṇe tathā ājuhāva mahīpālān bhīmo rājā svayaṃvare
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Then, when an auspicious time had arrived, on a holy lunar day and at a propitious moment, king Bhīma summoned the rulers of the earth for the svayaṃvara.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā pṛthivīpālāḥ sarve hṛcchayapīḍitāḥ tvaritāḥ samupājagmur damayantīm abhīpsavaḥ
english: Hearing that, all the rulers of the earth, tormented by the longing of their hearts, came hastening, eager to win Damayantī.

sanskrit: kanakastambharuciraṃ toraṇena virājitam viviśus te mahāraṅgaṃ nṛpāḥ siṃhā ivācalam
english: Those kings entered the great hall, resplendent with its archway and gleaming with golden pillars, like lions entering a mountain cave.

sanskrit: tatrāsaneṣu vividheṣv āsīnāḥ pṛthivīkṣitaḥ surabhisragdharāḥ sarve sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ
english: There the rulers of the earth were seated on various thrones, all wearing fragrant garlands, adorned with well-polished jewelled earrings.

sanskrit: tāṃ rājasamitiṃ pūrṇāṃ nāgair bhogavatīm iva saṃpūrṇāṃ puruṣavyāghrair vyāghrair giriguhām iva
english: That full assembly of kings was like Bhogavatī filled with serpents, or like a mountain cave filled with tigers — those tigers among men.

sanskrit: tatra sma pīnā dṛśyante bāhavaḥ parighopamāḥ ākāravantaḥ suślakṣṇāḥ pañcaśīrṣā ivoragāḥ
english: There could be seen massive arms like iron bars, well-shaped and very smooth, like five-headed serpents.

sanskrit: sukeśāntāni cārūṇi sunāsāni śubhāni ca mukhāni rājñāṃ śobhante nakṣatrāṇi yathā divi
english: The beautiful faces of the kings, with fine hair and handsome noses, shone like the constellations in the sky.

sanskrit: damayantī tato raṅgaṃ praviveśa śubhānanā muṣṇantī prabhayā rājñāṃ cakṣūṃṣi ca manāṃsi ca
english: Then Damayantī of the auspicious face entered the arena, stealing away with her radiance the eyes and minds of the kings.

sanskrit: tasyā gātreṣu patitā teṣāṃ dṛṣṭir mahātmanām tatra tatraiva saktābhūn na cacāla ca paśyatām
english: The gaze of those great-souled ones fell upon her limbs and remained fixed wherever it landed, unmoving in those who beheld her.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃkīrtyamāneṣu rājñāṃ nāmasu bhārata dadarśa bhaimī puruṣān pañca tulyākṛtīn iva
english: Then, O Bhārata, as the names of the kings were being proclaimed, the daughter of Bhīma saw five men who looked exactly alike.

sanskrit: tān samīkṣya tataḥ sarvān nirviśeṣākṛtīn sthitān saṃdehād atha vaidarbhī nābhyajānān nalaṃ nṛpam yaṃ yaṃ hi dadṛśe teṣāṃ taṃ taṃ mene nalaṃ nṛpam
english: Surveying them all, standing there indistinguishable in form, the princess of Vidarbha could not in her perplexity recognise king Nala — whichever one among them she looked at, she thought that one to be king Nala.

sanskrit: sā cintayantī buddhyātha tarkayām āsa bhāminī kathaṃ nu devāñ jānīyāṃ kathaṃ vidyāṃ nalaṃ nṛpam
english: She, thinking and reasoning with her mind, that spirited woman wondered: How shall I recognise the gods? How shall I know king Nala?

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintayantī sā vaidarbhī bhṛśaduḥkhitā śrutāni devaliṅgāni cintayām āsa bhārata
english: Thus thinking deeply, that princess of Vidarbha, greatly distressed, called to mind the marks of the gods that she had heard of, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: devānāṃ yāni liṅgāni sthavirebhyaḥ śrutāni me tānīha tiṣṭhatāṃ bhūmāv ekasyāpi na lakṣaye
english: "The marks of the gods that I have heard of from the elders — not a single one of those do I see on any of these five standing here on the ground."

sanskrit: sā viniścitya bahudhā vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ śaraṇaṃ prati devānāṃ prāptakālam amanyata
english: Having deliberated in many ways and considered again and again, she thought it was time to take refuge with the gods themselves.

sanskrit: vācā ca manasā caiva namaskāraṃ prayujya sā devebhyaḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā vepamānedam abravīt
english: With speech and with her mind she offered salutation; becoming trembling with joined palms before the gods, she spoke these words.

sanskrit: haṃsānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā yathā me naiṣadho vṛtaḥ patitve tena satyena devās taṃ pradiśantu me
english: "Having heard the message of the swans, I have chosen the king of Niṣadha as my husband — by that truth, let the gods point him out to me."
